Attn: Evelyn Thorne,

I am Barrister James Okafor, personal attorney to late Engr. Thomas Reinholt who died in a plane crash along with his wife and two children on the 4th of March 2019 leaving behind the sum of Eight Million Seven Hundred Thousand United States Dollars (USD 8,700,000.00) deposited with a Prime Bank here in Europe.

Since his death, i have made several enquiries to his embassy to locate any of my late client extended relatives but this has proved unsuccessful. After further investigation, it was disclosed that Mr Reinholt did not declare any next of kin in his official Bank Deposit documents and the said amount has now been declared UNCLAIMED by the Bank Management.

I am inviting you to stand in as the Next of Kin to my late client so that the fund of USD 8,700,000.00 can be paid to you, and we shall share the proceed at an agreed percentage. This is 100% risk free and legitimate as i have all legal documents to back up this claim, including the Certificate of Deposit, the Death Certificate of my late client, and a Letter of Administration issued by the probate registry.

Let me explain briefly how the process will work once you accept to proceed with me. First, I will file an application to the Bank Directorate of my late client, presenting you as the beneficiary and Next of Kin, backed by the aforementioned documents already in my possession. Second, upon approval, the Bank will issue us a Payment Approval Letter authorizing transfer of the funds into any bank account you nominate anywhere in the world. Third, I will personally travel to your country to conclude the sharing formalities once the funds have been confirmed received, so that everything is transparent between us and there is no ambiguity on either side.

I must state clearly that this transaction is 100% risk free to you, as I am a licensed Barrister and Notary Public and will use my professional standing to guarantee the process from beginning to end. All you need to provide at this stage is your consent to proceed, along with a few identification details so I can begin preparing the necessary paperwork on your behalf without delay.

If you find this business proposal reasonable, kindly respond immediately with the following:
1. Your Full Name and Contact Address
2. Direct Telephone Number
3. Occupation and Company Name
4. A copy of your International Passport or Driving License

Please treat this matter with the utmost confidentiality it deserves, as I am still bound by professional ethics as an attorney and cannot be seen to be soliciting outside proper legal channels. I have selected you carefully after a diligent search, and I trust that you will not betray this confidence once the funds are in your care, particularly regarding the percentage we agree upon.

I await your urgent response as time is not on our side, the Bank Compliance Department is under pressure to close all dormant accounts by end of quarter, after which unclaimed funds of this nature are transferred to the state treasury and become permanently unrecoverable by any next of kin, real or nominated.

Yours faithfully,
Barrister James Okafor
Attorney at Law
Tel: +44 703 195 8862
Email: barrister.j.okafor77@gmail.com

This is a private and confidential correspondence intended solely for the person to whom it is addressed. Please treat as strictly confidential and reply only to this email address.

subject: AME Insights: Q3 Lean Manufacturing Trends
snippet: AME INSIGHTS — Q3 2026 Welcome back to AME Insights, your quarterly digest on lean manufacturing and operational excellence trends across North America. RESHORING MOMENTUM CONTINUE
body_text:
AME INSIGHTS — Q3 2026

Welcome back to AME Insights, your quarterly digest on lean manufacturing and operational excellence trends across North America.

RESHORING MOMENTUM CONTINUES
Our latest member survey of 340 manufacturers shows 38% have reshored at least one product line in the past 18 months, up from 24% last year. The primary driver remains supply chain risk rather than pure cost — respondents cited lead-time volatility and single-source dependency as the top two concerns, ahead of labor cost differentials. For consultants advising clients on facility strategy, this suggests total-cost-of-ownership models that weight resilience alongside unit cost are increasingly what wins board approval.

WORKFORCE: THE SKILLS GAP ISN'T CLOSING
Despite record investment in automation, 61% of member plants report unfilled skilled-trades positions, with CNC machinists and industrial electricians the hardest to fill. Several members have had success with in-house apprenticeship programs partnered with community colleges — Ridgefield Manufacturing's program, profiled in this issue, cut time-to-productivity for new hires from 9 months to 5.

DIGITAL THREAD ADOPTION
Adoption of digital thread / MES integration remains uneven. Plants under 100 employees report only 22% adoption versus 58% for plants over 500 employees, largely due to upfront implementation cost and lack of internal IT resources. This is a real opportunity area for outside advisors who can de-risk the business case and phase implementation around cash flow constraints rather than a big-bang rollout.

UPCOMING EVENTS
- AME 2026 Chicago Summit, October 6-9, McCormick Place
- Regional Lean Roundtable (Midwest chapter), September 12, Rockford IL
- Webinar: "Building the Business Case for Digital Thread," August 28

MEMBER SPOTLIGHT
This quarter we profile a mid-market automotive supplier that cut changeover time 34% through a SMED initiative led by an outside consulting team — a useful case study to reference with clients weighing whether outside help is worth the fee. The engagement ran 14 weeks, involved three plant floor workshops, and the client credits the outside facilitator with getting operators to buy in where two prior internal attempts had stalled. We also spotlight a packaging manufacturer that used a rolling six-week diagnostic before committing to a larger transformation program, a structure several members have told us they're now requesting explicitly from their advisors rather than accepting a full-scope proposal up front.

CHAPTER NEWS
The Midwest chapter welcomes two new board members this quarter, both plant operations leaders from member companies. The chapter's fall calendar includes plant tours, a benchmarking roundtable on labor cost trends, and a joint session with the local ASCM chapter on integrating lean and supply chain planning — a combination several consulting members have asked us to cover more often given how frequently the two disciplines show up together in client engagements.

CERTIFICATION UPDATES
The Lean Bronze Certification exam window opens again in September, and early registration discounts are available for members through August 31. AME is also piloting a new credential aimed specifically at external advisors and consultants, recognizing that a growing share of our membership works client-side rather than as in-house practitioners. If that's a track you'd find useful, reply to this email — we're collecting interest before finalizing the curriculum.

RESEARCH NOTE
A recurring theme in this quarter's member interviews: leadership teams are asking for faster proof of ROI before greenlighting the next phase of any improvement program, a shift from the multi-year transformation roadmaps common a few years ago. Advisors who can show measurable wins within a single quarter are reporting stronger renewal rates on follow-on work.

As always, thank you for being an AME member. Questions or story ideas for future issues can be sent to insights@ame.org.

AME Insights Editorial Team
Association for Manufacturing Excellence

subject: IndustryWeek Executive Briefing
snippet: IN THIS ISSUE FEATURE: Why Fixed-Fee Consulting Engagements Are Replacing Time-and-Materials in Manufacturing As manufacturers grow wary of open-ended consulting spend, a growing s
body_text:
IN THIS ISSUE

FEATURE: Why Fixed-Fee Consulting Engagements Are Replacing Time-and-Materials in Manufacturing
As manufacturers grow wary of open-ended consulting spend, a growing share of operations engagements are structured as fixed-fee, milestone-based contracts. We spoke with three boutique advisory firms about how they scope and price this way without eating the risk of scope creep — a theme worth watching if your own engagements are trending the same direction.

DATA: Q2 industrial production ticked up 1.4% quarter over quarter, driven largely by durable goods. Capacity utilization remains below the 15-year average, suggesting continued appetite for efficiency-focused consulting engagements over pure capacity expansion.

PEOPLE MOVES: Ridgefield Mfg names a new VP of Operations; three other executive moves across the Midwest manufacturing corridor.

TOOLS: A roundup of five ERP add-ons gaining traction with mid-market manufacturers this quarter, including two aimed specifically at improving forecast accuracy for make-to-order shops. Several readers wrote in after last month's issue asking for more detail on implementation timelines, so this roundup includes real customer-reported rollout windows rather than vendor marketing estimates — most ran 4 to 7 months longer than initially quoted, a pattern worth flagging to any client currently evaluating a system change.

DEEP DIVE: THE CONSULTANT'S ROLE IN CAPEX DECISIONS
A growing number of manufacturers are bringing outside advisors into capital equipment decisions earlier than in past cycles, not just for post-purchase process design. We interviewed five plant-level finance leaders who described a shift from "call the consultant once the machine is installed" to "get a second opinion before the PO is cut." For advisory firms, this means capex evaluation frameworks and vendor-neutral ROI modeling are becoming a more explicit part of the sales conversation, not an afterthought bundled into a broader engagement.

LABOR MARKET WATCH: Wage growth for skilled manufacturing roles held at 5.8% year over year in the Midwest, slightly ahead of the national average. Several members report that overtime costs, not base wage inflation, are now the bigger line-item pressure, driven by continued difficulty filling second and third shifts.

READER MAILBAG: A plant manager in Indiana wrote in asking how peers are structuring fixed-fee versus time-and-materials contracts with outside consultants on multi-phase projects. We're compiling responses for a future issue — reply if you have a structure that's worked well for your organization.

EVENTS CALENDAR: A full list of manufacturing conferences and webinars through year-end, including several with consulting-firm delegate rates.

Read the full briefing at industryweek.com/briefing

IndustryWeek Editorial
body_html:
IN THIS ISSUE

FEATURE: Why Fixed-Fee Consulting Engagements Are Replacing Time-and-Materials in Manufacturing
As manufacturers grow wary of open-ended consulting spend, a growing share of operations engagements are structured as fixed-fee, milestone-based contracts. We spoke with three boutique advisory firms about how they scope and price this way without eating the risk of scope creep — a theme worth watching if your own engagements are trending the same direction.

DATA: Q2 industrial production ticked up 1.4% quarter over quarter, driven largely by durable goods. Capacity utilization remains below the 15-year average, suggesting continued appetite for efficiency-focused consulting engagements over pure capacity expansion.

PEOPLE MOVES: Ridgefield Mfg names a new VP of Operations; three other executive moves across the Midwest manufacturing corridor.

TOOLS: A roundup of five ERP add-ons gaining traction with mid-market manufacturers this quarter, including two aimed specifically at improving forecast accuracy for make-to-order shops. Several readers wrote in after last month's issue asking for more detail on implementation timelines, so this roundup includes real customer-reported rollout windows rather than vendor marketing estimates — most ran 4 to 7 months longer than initially quoted, a pattern worth flagging to any client currently evaluating a system change.

DEEP DIVE: THE CONSULTANT'S ROLE IN CAPEX DECISIONS
A growing number of manufacturers are bringing outside advisors into capital equipment decisions earlier than in past cycles, not just for post-purchase process design. We interviewed five plant-level finance leaders who described a shift from "call the consultant once the machine is installed" to "get a second opinion before the PO is cut." For advisory firms, this means capex evaluation frameworks and vendor-neutral ROI modeling are becoming a more explicit part of the sales conversation, not an afterthought bundled into a broader engagement.

LABOR MARKET WATCH: Wage growth for skilled manufacturing roles held at 5.8% year over year in the Midwest, slightly ahead of the national average. Several members report that overtime costs, not base wage inflation, are now the bigger line-item pressure, driven by continued difficulty filling second and third shifts.

READER MAILBAG: A plant manager in Indiana wrote in asking how peers are structuring fixed-fee versus time-and-materials contracts with outside consultants on multi-phase projects. We're compiling responses for a future issue — reply if you have a structure that's worked well for your organization.

EVENTS CALENDAR: A full list of manufacturing conferences and webinars through year-end, including several with consulting-firm delegate rates.
